summary: The core numerics look internally consistent: I re-derived the published 80.32/82.36/83.02/83.55/86.56% fixed-`(mu,nu)` degradations, and a quick profile-wise `mu` re-optimization on the existing `nu_ratio=0.2` grid still gives about 84.25/84.43/84.73/87.37% at 25/50/100/150 km, so the large drop does not look like a mismatched-`μ/ν` methodology bug. `DeviceProfile` also maps cleanly into `FibreChannel`. I did not find material security, performance, or runtime error-handling defects, but the patch should still fail this round because the main regression test is far too weak to protect the documented S2.3 finding. I could not run `pytest` in this sandbox because there is no writable temp directory, so verification was by direct Python calls plus static review.

issues.description: `test_device_imperfection_degrades_rate` only asserts `degradation_pct > 10.0`, even though this delivery's headline result is ~80-87% degradation and the original plan expected 20-50%. A regression from the current ~83% down to 15% would still pass, so the test does not meaningfully guard the acceptance claim or the documented `[FIND]`.
issues.suggestion: Raise the lower bound to something that protects the actual result, e.g. `>= 50%` as the proposed revised lower bound, or at minimum `>= 20%` if you want to stay aligned with the current plan wording. Prefer checking several representative distances (25/50/100/150 km) instead of only 50 km.

issues.description: The findings document frames the 80-87% result as a Pareto-front degradation, but the published table is a fixed `mu=0.5, nu=0.1` slice, and the only optimization sweep is an LMC-only `mu` scan with fixed `nu_ratio=0.2`. Because `ideal` and `typical` peak at materially different `mu` values, the wording overstates what was actually measured; section 5 also omits this limitation.
issues.suggestion: Either relabel the headline result as a fixed-intensity comparison, or add an explicit profile-wise optimized comparison before using it to justify a plan revision. Also add a limitation noting that the delivered evidence is a 19-point slice plus a 205-point LMC-only scan, not a full `>=1000`-point Pareto-front study.

issues.description: The `mu_best = 0.42` claim is more precise than the data support. On a finer 0.005 scan around the optimum, the LMC best point shifts to `0.415` at 50-100 km and `0.41` at 125 km, with a very flat plateau around `0.41-0.42`; the current text makes this look like an exact, distance-invariant constant rather than a coarse-grid plateau.
issues.suggestion: Rephrase this to `mu_best ≈ 0.41-0.42` or 'near 0.42', and add an explicit caveat that the value depends on grid resolution and the fixed `nu_ratio=0.2` assumption.

round_recommendation: Tighten the degradation regression test first, then revise the findings/log wording so the 80-87% result is clearly labeled as fixed-intensity evidence and the `μ` optimum is stated as an approximate plateau rather than an exact universal constant.
